info.desc: Transformer is the second solo studio album by American recording artist Lou Reed. Produced by David Bowie and Mick Ronson, the album was released in November 1972 by RCA Records. It is considered an influential landmark of the glam rock genre, anchored by Reed's most successful single, "Walk on the Wild Side", which touched on then-controversial topics of sexual orientation, gender identity, prostitution, and drug use. Though Reed's self-titled debut solo album had been unsuccessful, Bowie had been an early fan of Reed's former band The Velvet Underground, and used his own fame to promote Reed, who had not yet .

podcast.body: Released in 1972, this album was produced by David Bowie and his Spiders From Mars guitarist, Mick Ronson, who helped Lou Reed develop a new sound. Three of its songs were initially commissioned by Andy Warhol for a Broadway musical he was attempting to stage. To everyone's surprise, the album yielded a genuine Top 40 hit, "Walk on the Wild Side," despite its explicit lyrics. "Bowie and his spiders from Mars guitarist, Mick Ronson, helped Lou find a new sound. The result was a record called Transformer in 1972."

podcast.body: Released merely five months after his debut album, this is considered the most important album of Lou Reed's career. It was recorded very quickly, partly because it contained at least four songs that had already been composed and recorded during the Velvet Underground era. The album was funded by David Bowie and produced by Bowie himself, alongside Mick Ronson, Bowie's guitarist. "El Transformer, con diferencia de algún más importante de su carrera."

podcast.body: The album's themes encompass not only discarded Velvet Underground recordings but also Lou Reed's personal experiences at Andy Warhol's Factory, recounting "macabre stories" from that period. Despite maintaining the same controversial, explicit, and censorable themes as his first album, it achieved "incredible success," largely attributed to the boost provided by David Bowie's involvement. This success officially launched Lou Reed's solo career. "Todo el disco nos viene a contar esas macabras historias que tenía Luric sobre lo que se cocian en la factoria."

podcast.body: This album featured the hit song "Walk on the Wild Side," which explicitly name-checked real-life characters from Andy Warhol's circle. The song's portrayal of various sexualities and gender roles made it a landmark in popular culture, especially surprising as it became a major Top 40 radio hit in 1972 despite its lyrical content. "This song, surprisingly, shockingly, was a major top 40 hit."
